summary.headline: Sharda Motor Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% to INR1,011.1 crores, but gross profit grew only 8% to INR203.9 crores and EBITDA 5% to INR103.2 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 34% YoY to INR1,011.1 crores, driven by pass-through catalyst sales and product mix, while gross profit grew 8% to INR203.9 crores. Management attributed the weak gross profit growth to a supplier fire at a key customer and one-time premium raw material and freight costs linked to the geopolitical situation in April and May, which it said stabilised in July. EBITDA was INR103.2 crores (10.2% margin, up 5%), and PAT was INR86.5 crores. Management said the lightweighting, export and emission order book is moving into SOPs, but gave no numerical guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: PBT before exceptional items (after JV and associate share)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR107.7 crores last year, which excluded INR22.4 crores exceptional gains

segments.name: Lightweighting (control arms, links, subframes, torsion beams)
segments.commentary: Previously announced control arm and link programmes continue to ramp up. Donghee licence extends the portfolio into subframes and torsion beams, with RFQs generated for multiple platforms. Management sized the broader lightweighting portfolio at INR8,000-9,000 crores in about 5 years, with a target share of mid-teen to high-teen percentage.

segments.name: Emissions and adjacencies
segments.commentary: Multiple WLTP replacement orders secured from leading passenger vehicle OEMs in Q1. The temperature-controlled tube order for an off-highway equipment maker has begun SOP and is ramping up as planned.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Three North American engine and genset orders with combined annual value of about US$10.7 million and lifetime value of about US$58.5 million; SOPs expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27. Management declined to quantify FY27 or FY28 revenue from these orders.

segments.name: Purem JV (CV above 4 litres)
segments.commentary: Stable and profitable. A new programme started in Q4 FY26 and will ramp up through FY27. Sharda receives 50% of PAT and is not in management control.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given. Management said the exact quarterly trajectory depends on customer production schedules, SOPs and programme ramp-ups.

FY27 growth drivers cited: full-year benefit of lightweighting orders, ramp-up of additional lightweighting programmes, temperature-controlled tube adjacencies, North American export SOPs, and supportive domestic OEM volumes.

Management said it is now ready to be more assertive on acquisitions, subject to filters for strategic fit, valuation, integration and ROCE. Capital will be split between organic growth, technology partnerships, acquisitions and shareholder returns.
Management said it expects the lightweighting market share, last measured at 14% at FY26 end, to rise. The number will be calculated only at FY27 year-end.
capex_capacity: Chakan 3 lightweighting facility has started SOP and is ramping up in line with customer schedules; capacity is modular and tied to confirmed programmes.
New Uttarakhand facility, about INR20 crores investment, is progressing per the customer plan. It will co-locate relocated business first and later serve other North India customers.
Utilisation is expected to rise progressively as the announced control arm and link orders ramp up.
demand_pricing: Management cited industry domestic production up over 22% YoY to 93.6 lakh units. Passenger vehicle production rose 16.8% to 14.53 lakh units and utility vehicles rose 21.2%. LCV production rose 20.8% to 1.91 lakh units.
Management said the addressable market grew 8-10%, and Sharda's gross profit growth of 8% was broadly in line. The company is not present with Japanese OEMs, which it adjusts for.

Substrate (catalyst) prices are customer-directed and passed through without lag. Other direct materials are indexed with a one-to-two-quarter lag. Steel and aluminium impact was said to be immaterial to gross profit.

CAFE III draft (16 July 2026, proposed from 1 April 2027) and BS6.3/WLTP from 1 April 2027 expected to lift emission content. BS7 is not yet notified; Euro-7-aligned content would rise in hot-end aftertreatment, catalyst loading and GPF.
Premium two-wheeler emission opportunity under evaluation for domestic supply (above a particular cc). TREM3 integrated muffler market estimated at INR60-100 crores, which management called small.

qa_highlights.question: Can export orders be converted into FY27 and FY28 top-line, for example about INR100 crores in FY27 and INR200 crores in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers, saying revenue depends on customer schedules. It said SOP dates are unchanged and a new platform usually takes one to two years to reach peak volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Gross profit growth of 8% versus steel and aluminium price increases: is there a one-quarter lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said catalyst and substrate are fully pass-through without lag. Other direct materials are indexed on a one-to-two-quarter lag, and one-time premium freight and RM costs were absorbed in Q1. It said the impact was built into the 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is growth lagging the industry, and when will it converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the serviceable market grew 8-10% after adjusting for the Japanese OEM exposure and a supplier fire at a key customer, and Sharda grew 8%. Growth drivers are existing orders, RFQ conversion and industry growth. No guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Donghee TLA opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Joint showcasing to OEMs has generated RFQs across multiple platforms. Management sized the broader lightweighting portfolio at INR8,000-9,000 crores in about 5 years, and targets a mid-teen to high-teen percentage share.

qa_highlights.question: What content uplift comes from BS6.3, CAFE III and BS7?
qa_highlights.answer: WLTP content uplift may be limited because catalyst efficiency and calibration change rather than a full redesign. BS7 content would rise through hot-end aftertreatment, high catalyst loading and GPF, but depends on Euro-7 adoption. CAFE III supports lightweighting and multi-powertrain engineered emission systems.

qa_highlights.question: What is the emission export pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the export focus is CV emission components, temperature-controlled tubes, genset emission components and small agri genset exhaust systems. It pointed to announced orders across emissions, agri and tubes, and said no pipeline figures would be given.

risks_watch: Gross profit growth of 8% against 34% revenue growth shows pass-through dilution; the Q2 gross margin trend needs watching as one-time costs normalise.
The supplier fire at a key customer affected Q1 production; recovery timing was not disclosed.
Management said the one-to-two-quarter raw material indexing lag can shift timing, though it claimed no net vacuum.
Export SOPs for the North American orders are due in Q3 and Q4 FY27, and the timing of revenue ramp was not quantified.
The lightweighting market share gain (from 14%) will only be disclosed at FY27 year-end.
Geopolitical risk and premium raw material procurement costs are flagged as ongoing risks.
Management said it is ready for larger acquisitions, but no target or timeline was given.
key_quotes: So, giving a number is going to be a little difficult because this would depend upon the customer schedules.
These were because of the geopolitical situation in April and May. In July, these have already stabilized.
So, we are broadly growing in line with the industry.
Having established these capabilities, we believe we are now ready to be more assertive in pursuing strategic acquisitions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, the order book and long-term strategy, but cautious on quantification: management declined to give revenue, ramp-up or market-share numbers for exports, lightweighting and emissions, citing customer schedules. Gross profit growth was explained defensively, with the supplier fire and one-time premium raw material and freight costs blamed, and the raw material pass-through lag was answered inconsistently across questions.

growth.why: No numerical FY27 guidance was given; management cited lightweighting order ramp-ups, three North American export orders (US$10.7m annual, SOPs Q3-Q4 FY27) and domestic OEM volumes as drivers, with Chakan 3 at SOP and modular capacity tied to confirmed programmes, but declined to quantify FY27 revenue.
